chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Uthman ibn Isa, raising it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), said:

He was asked about a man to whom his father had gifted a slave girl, so he made her give birth (to children), and she remained with him for a time. Then she mentioned that his father had slept with her before he had gifted her to him, so he kept aside from her. He said: 'She should not be ratified (as free/owned by him exclusively via the child-bearing process).'

key_terms.أَوْلَدَهَا: He made her give birth / she bore children
key_terms.فَاجْتَنَبَهَا: So he kept aside from her / separated
key_terms.وَطِئَهَا: He slept with her / had intercourse with her

ai.seo_question: What is the legal ruling when a father sleeps with a slave girl before gifting her to his son?
ai.summary: In this ruling from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) addresses the legal status of a slave girl gifted by her father to her brother after she bore his child. The phrase 'لَا تُصَدَّقُ' is interpreted by Shia jurists to mean that the act of emancipation (itq) via child-bearing (umm al-walad) is not validated or recognized in this specific context, likely because the father's prior sexual relationship with her before the gift created a legal impediment to the transfer of full ownership rights necessary for the son's claim. This highlights the nuanced Shia jurisprudence on how prior marital or concubine relations affect the validity of gifts and subsequent emancipation statuses within the family structure.
